correctness.rationale: The two negative signs have product +1; gauging them away turns M into the sum with two constant sign blocks. The periodic zero-field covariance C_d=(t^d+t^(n−d))/(1+t^n) follows by summing the two arcs. Subtracting four times the unordered cross-block sum from the all-plus quadratic form gives the stated formula; its only separation-dependent factor increases strictly to the midpoint. The endpoints follow from independent spins and perfect alignment after the gauge transform. In the balanced even case the initial derivative 2−8/n is positive for n≥6. Substitution t=exp(−x/n) gives compact-uniform convergence to Phi; writing y=x/2 gives Phi=tanh(y)[y−2 tanh(y/2)]/y²>0. Since the sign vector sums to zero and sech(x/2)≤C_d≤1, the normalized variance is bounded by 1−sech(x/2) at small x, and the unsigned ferromagnetic sum gives 2/x+2/n at large x. Thus maximizers cannot escape either end and the claimed global peak limit follows. An independent exact Gibbs enumeration (branches/f46fed5e-024d-4562-afe4-f6fffa991fc3/independent_check.py) matched 66 cases for n=4 to 9 and t=1/3,1/2; the numerical peak orientation was independently reproduced, not certified as unique. The peak is for X=chi/beta, not chi.
